result:
I would eliminate the fundamental isolation of the human mind—specifically, the inability of one person to truly experience the subjective reality of another.

Right now, every human is locked inside their own skull. You can describe your pain, your grief, your joy, or your exhaustion, but no one else can actually *inhabit* it. That gap—the distance between what you feel and what someone else perceives—is the quiet source of almost every human-made catastrophe. 

It is what makes dehumanization possible. It allows people to reduce others to statistics, political enemies, or abstract concepts. Cruelty relies almost entirely on a failure of imagination, on the convenience of not having to feel the weight of what you inflict or ignore.

If humans had a natural, unavoidable sense that allowed them to briefly and viscerally feel the emotional and physical reality of the person in front of them, deliberate cruelty would become functionally impossible, because harming another would be indistinguishable from harming oneself.

It wouldn't fix every problem. It wouldn't stop disease, scarcity, or natural death. But it would strip away the armor of indifference, destroy the utility of malice, and make genuine understanding the baseline of human existence rather than a rare achievement.
